notes: First attempt PASSED (200) — no retries needed. Used q[folder_ids]=764093 (the __readonly__ pool folder) rather than free-text q[query], since guidance warns special characters are stripped before matching and identifiers like 'TC-54455' were not a safe bet for a text match; folder scoping deterministically hit the two known fixture cases (TC-54455 'probe case A', TC-54456 'probe case B') and exercised the full item shape, including nested case_type/priority/status/automation_state option objects and an attachments array on one row. Verdict is DRIFT, not PASS, because of two real contract mismatches: (1) every row declares comments_count but no row actually returns it (declared_missing), and (2) `folders` is declared as a flat array of rich folder objects but is actually returned as a map keyed by folder id whose values are a different, trimmer shape — a structural type mismatch (array vs object), not just extra/missing fields. There is also a long tail of undeclared-but-returned item fields (automation_state as a full option object, attachments, template_id/name/step_type, step_count, is_shared, the two test_run_results_* nulls, test_case_dataset, and value_category/valueDetails nested inside case_type/priority/status) — none of these break usage but the declared schema undercounts what the row actually contains. describeCapability for v1 never surfaced a `json_path` key on any parameter (despite include_responses=all and the entity being marked shape:'discovered'), so contract.json_path is null here — that's a v1-only gap, not an omission on my part. On the v1-vs-v2 question: I also pulled the v2 contract (search_project_entities_by_filter, POST body) purely to compare — no invoke against it, staying read-only and in-scope. Beyond GET-vs-POST, v2 is a materially richer filter language, not just the same filters moved into a body for length reasons: it adds `match` (a per-field boolean-operator map — all/any/none — for combining a field's own values), `empty` (is-unset filters keyed by system_fields/custom_fields), first-class `custom_fields` value matching, direct `ids` fetch, `is_archived`, `issue_type`/`issue_ids`, `last_executed_by`, and an absolute `date_range` in epoch-ms (v1's created_at/updated_at only take the relative <n>_<unit> token or 'all_time'). v1's flat q[...] bracket params cannot express boolean composition (AND/OR/NONE across a single field's multiple values) or is-empty checks at all — that's the real separation, not just query-string-length avoidance. Every v2 body field also carries an explicit json_path (/q/<name> or /required/<name>), which v1 params never do. So the routing-eval finding that they're 'near-indistinguishable' holds for the common filter surface (folder/status/priority/case_type/owner/tags/automation_state/created_at/updated_at all exist on both with equivalent semantics), but diverges once `match`/`empty`/`custom_fields`/`ids`/`is_archived` are needed — those only exist on v2.
